title: Fish, bass, baked or broiled, coated

content.title: About
content.content: Bass is a freshwater fish from the perch family, prized for its tender white flesh, low fat content, and mild flavor. When baked or broiled with a coating, the fish stays moist while the crust adds a satisfying crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bass can grow up to 60 cm and weigh over 2 kg, but most market portions are fillets of 150–250 g.
Coatings often combine breadcrumbs, flour, herbs, and spices to enhance aroma and texture.
Baking at 180–200 °C preserves most B‑vitamins, while quick broiling creates a golden crust.
Bass is commonly served with lemon, fresh herbs (parsley, dill) and a light yogurt or cream sauce.
In many households bass is considered a “go‑to” fish because of its availability and ease of preparation.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Bass provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, mostly polyunsaturated.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12, B6 and niacin aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and phosphorus
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant; phosphorus is essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than in fatty fish, bass still supplies EPA and DHA.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Freshwater bass can accumulate cadmium or mercury, so moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: High sodium in coating
items.content: Salty breading can increase sodium intake, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Proper cooking
items.content: Undercooked fish may harbor pathogens; cook to an internal temperature of 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coat bass fillets in a mixture of breadcrumbs, spices, and a drizzle of olive oil, then bake 15–20 minutes at 200 °C or broil until golden. Serve with lemon wedges, fresh herbs, and a light vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh fillets in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Frozen fillets store at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen fish in the fridge, not at room temperature.
